text:
incident-bot: PAGING: hosted-runtime - kvmap growth alarm (severity: high). Memory alarm on shard hosted-usw2-a. Pager: devon (oncall).

devon: acked. i'm on it — pulling traces + metrics now. anyone already looked at recent deploys?

ops-bot: recent deploy: runtime v3.14.2 rolled 12m ago; config change: prefetch_max_entries=5k -> 50k (intent: prefetch boost), continuous_batching window increased = 250ms -> 500ms.

aj: ugh that prefetch bump rings bell. seeing kvmap entries explode in the last 8m. prom query: `sum(kvmap_entries) by (shard)` shows spike ~10x.

natalie: logs show repeated long prompts from a customer causing prefix amplification. example: `session_id=abc123 prefix_len=128K tokens` then repeated streaming -> kvmap insertion churn.

devon: collecting heap snapshot from gpu host. current: `gpu0_mem=96%`, `kvmap_bytes=82.3GB`, `kvmap_entries=13,120,341`. OOMs starting at 2423456755.

kevin: customers impacted: a subset of hosted-chat customers in us-west-2  — ~0.8% of requests returning 5xx (OOM / runtime-reject). Latency also spiked for others as batching collapsed.

sara: first mitigation idea: throttle prefetch + reduce continuous_batching window to 100ms and enable aggressive eviction (lru_age=30s) for canary shard. patch command below:
```bash
# canary patch
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.runtime/shard/hosted-usw2-a/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefetch_max_entries":5000, "continuous_batching_ms":100, "kvmap_eviction_lru_age_s":30}'
```

devon: applying to canary now. will monitor memory and error rates.

ops-bot: canary applied to hosted-usw2-a-01 at 2423456783.

aj: after canary patch: `kvmap_entries` on canary decreased from 13M -> 2.1M in ~22s. memory fell to ~68%. error rate on that shard down to baseline. good sign.

natalie: rolling to the rest of hosted-usw2-a with staged batch of 3 machines. patch script: `./admin-rollout --shard hosted-usw2-a --group-size 3 --wait-healthy 45s`

devon: rolling now. lowering prefetch across region and setting temporary global guard: `max_kvmap_bytes=40GB`. This prevents other shards from hitting OOM while we investigate root cause.

kevin: customer comms: Ops, please prepare short note: impacted customers may have seen failed responses and higher latencies between 12:04-12:12 UTC. we should offer retries/credits.

sara: sending short comms draft to #support-digest. cc'ing devon.

incident-bot: ALERT: rollback candidate detected for runtime v3.14.2 (older v3.14.1 was stable). devon, do we want rollback?

devon: not yet — the config hotpatch is low-risk and already shows improvement. rollback would be wider disruption. let's stabilize and then decide.

aj: still seeing a small cluster (~2 nodes) lag behind due to stuck GC. manual restart recommended if they don't recover in 2m.

devon: restarted the two nodes. both came back healthy. global error rate back to normal after full rollout (~12:09 UTC).

natalie: note: root cause hypothesis: prefetch_max_entries increase combined with longer batching allowed large prefixes to stay cached longer; when a few sessions submitted extremely long prompts (prefix amplification) the kvmap growth became multiplicative. we'll need a proper guardrail in runtime to cap per-session prefix bytes.

kevin: agreed. immediate follow-ups: 1) revert prefetch bump in config repo, 2) add per-session kvmap cap (e.g. 8MB), 3) add metric + alert for per-session kvmap growth, 4) postmortem.

sara: i'm taking postmortem writeup. devon handing incident to sara for follow-up tasks and blameless postmortem. devon — any final notes before handoff?

devon: thanks — key timeline: deploy 12:02 UTC -> kvmap spike 12:05 -> OOMs 12:07 -> canary patch 12:08 -> full rollout 12:09 -> stabilized 12:11. No data exfiltration, no customer data lost.

ops-bot: incident closed (stabilized). severity: sev2 -> follow-up required.

sara: handing over. i'll schedule postmortem runbook + action items. tagging @support for comms. :handshake:
